Starting from $x_0=0$, induction gives $x_k=\omega\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(I-\omega T)^jA^*y_\delta$: the sum is empty for $k=0$, and multiplying the $k$-term sum by $I-\omega T$ and adding $\omega A^*y_\delta$ produces the $(k+1)$-term sum.

Applying [F2] to invert $B_k$ proves the stated identity.

entries.exact_source_assertion: For $k\ge1$, the scalar geometric identity gives $g_k(t)=[1-(1-\omega t)^k]/t$ for $t>0$. Since $|1-\omega t|\le1$, both the bound by $2$ and the finite-sum bound by $k\omega t$ hold for its numerator. Hence $$\sqrt t\,|g_k(t)|\le\min\{2/\sqrt t,\omega k\sqrt t\}\le\sqrt{2\omega k}.$$ The last inequality follows by splitting at $t=2/(\omega k)$. For $Q_k=g_k(T)A^*$, adjoint multiplication gives $Q_kQ_k^*=g_k(T)Tg_k(T)^*$, the compact spectral multiplier with scalar values $t|g_k(t)|^2$ and value zero on $\ker T$. [F7] bounds its norm by the supremum of these values; [F4] and $\|Q_k\|^2=\|Q_kQ_k^*\|$ then give $\|Q_k\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}$. Applying [F1] to $y_\delta-y$ gives $\|x_k^\delta-x_k\|=\|Q_k(y_\delta-y)\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta$.

entries.exact_source_assertion:
Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of
[[thm-landweber-source-and-noise-error-bounds]]. Let
$x^\dagger=T^\nu w$ with $0<\nu\le1$ and $R=\|w\|\ge0$. Fix $\tau>1$ and
$\delta>0$ with $\|y_\delta-Ax^\dagger\|\le\delta$. Let $k_\delta$ be the
first index on the associated infinite mathematical path satisfying
$\|Ax_{k_\delta}^\delta-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, where $x_k^\delta$ is
the corresponding noisy-data path.
If a finite budget is used, assume it is at least the upper bound $K_\delta$
constructed in the proof when $R>0$. If $R=0$, the initial iterate is the
first crossing and any finite budget suffices. For all sufficiently small
$\delta$,
$$\|x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger\| \le C_{\nu,A,\omega,\tau}R^{1/(2\nu+1)}\delta^{2\nu/(2\nu+1)}.$$
The conclusion is conditional on an actual discrepancy crossing; a budget
exhaustion status is inconclusive.

entries.exact_source_assertion: Its scalar matrix is $B_1=(N^{-2})$ and right-hand side is $\beta_1e_1=N^{-1}e_1$, so the unique minimizer is $z_1=N$. Consequently $x_1^\delta=x_0+Nv_1=(0,N)^T$, $A_Nx_1^\delta=y^\delta$, and $\|x_1^\delta-x^\dagger\|_2=N$. The noise is $\|y^\delta-y\|_2=N^{-1}$, so the error-to-noise ratio is $N^2\to\infty$. This refutes the proposed uniform bound and shows that the projected solve can fit a small noise component in a weak singular direction. The terminal $\beta_2=0$ is the algorithm's breakdown branch after the projected iterate has been formed, so this calculation does not invoke a nonbreakdown theorem.

entries.exact_source_assertion: Here $A^*A e_j=4^{-j}e_j$. Substituting into [F2] gives $x_{k,j}^\delta=\delta2^{j/2}\bigl(1-(1-4^{-j})^k\bigr)$. For an integer $n\ge2$, Bernoulli's inequality gives $(1+1/(n-1))^n\ge1+n/(n-1)>2$, hence $(1-1/n)^n<1/2$. Taking $n=4^j$ shows $|x_{k_j,j}^\delta|\ge\delta2^{j/2}/2$, which tends to infinity. Thus $\|x_{k_j}^\delta-x^\dagger\|\to\infty$ although the residual tends to zero; this is semiconvergence and shows why the method needs an explicit stopping rule.
